info.description:
This documentation describes the Source Code API.

Source Code: Git Repository Management Service

Source Code is a platform designed for centralized interaction with Git repositories, built to facilitate efficient collaborative software development. The service provides the functionality necessary for development teams to organize, manage, and control the development process, regardless of the chosen methodology.

Key Features:

•  Collaborative Development: Source Code offers tools and features to support team-based code collaboration, accommodating various workflows commonly adopted by development teams.
•  Public API: Source Code exposes a public API for automating routine tasks and integrating with other development tools. This enables the configuration of CI/CD pipelines, automated code review processes, and more.

Core Entities:

•  Project: A global container that groups repositories and encompasses shared settings. The Project represents the highest level of organization within Source Code.
•  Repository: A storage location for source code, containing the history of changes, branches, and other artifacts required for development.
•  Repository Settings: Configuration parameters defining the rules and policies governing interaction with the repository, including branch settings, hooks, and integrations.
•  Pull Request: A mechanism for proposing code changes, facilitating code review and discussion before integrating modifications into the main branch. Pull Requests are crucial for maintaining code quality and ensuring team consensus.
•  Webhook: A callback mechanism that allows the Source Code service to notify external systems about events occurring within repositories. Webhooks are configured for specific triggers (e.g., pull request creation, push to a branch) and enable integration with other tools and services.
•  User: An authenticated account possessing access rights and permissions within the Source Code project.

Business Entities:

•  Issue: An entity representing a task or problem related to the project. Issues can be linked to pull requests and branches to track progress and development context.
•  Label: An entity used for categorizing and classifying projects, pull requests, and issues. Labels facilitate the organization and filtering of information and enable priority assignment.
•  Service Account: An account intended for use by services and applications for secure inter-service communication. Service Accounts enable task automation and provide authorization without user intervention.
•  Notification Subscription: A mechanism that allows users to receive notifications about changes and events occurring with tracked entities. Notifications can be delivered through the service interface ("bell icon") and via email.

System Entities (Technical Components):

•  Health Endpoint: An endpoint providing information about the service's current state and availability. Used for monitoring the health of Source Code.
•  Job: An entity representing a unit of work executed by workers. Jobs are used for asynchronous data processing and execution of resource-intensive operations.
•  Git Repository Bundle: An entity used for configuring and managing Git repository bundles. Bundles enable efficient transfer and synchronization of large repository data volumes.

For example, let's look at a request that is authorized, receives a token, and uses this token to verify the health of the service.

```bash
simple positive case:
AUTH_USERNAME="sfera-admin"
AUTH_PASSWORD="sfera-admin"
HOST="https://sfera-t1.ru"

ACCESS_TOKEN=$(curl -ks -X POST "${HOST}/api/auth/login" \
H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"username\":\"$AUTH_USERNAME\",\"password\":\"$AUTH_PASSWORD\"}" \
 sed -n 's/.*"access_token":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')

curl -k "${HOST}/app/sourcecode/api/api/v2/health" \
H 'Accept: */*' \
H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

Important note: all work with plug-ins, code coverage with tests and other things that affect the quality of the code is in the Quality Code service and described in the documentation. {HOST}/quality-api/swagger-ui/index.html
